title: Minimum Operations to Make Elements Within K Subarrays Equal
summary: Given an integer array nums and two integers x and k, find the minimum number of operations required to make at least k non-overlapping subarrays of size exactly x have all elements equal.
statement: Given an integer array nums and two integers x and k, find the minimum number of operations required to make at least k non-overlapping subarrays of size exactly x have all elements equal. You can perform operations by increasing or decreasing any element of nums by 1 any number of times.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 integers; 2 <= x and k*x <= len(nums); k <= 15.
One operation changes one value by one. Choose at least k non-overlapping length-x subarrays whose values become equal within each chosen subarray.
Different chosen subarrays may use different final values; minimize the total operations.
hints: A fixed window is cheapest to equalize at a median; after computing every window cost, the remaining choice is weighted non-overlapping interval DP.
Maintain window counts and sums in Fenwick trees to obtain a median and absolute-distance cost in logarithmic time.
Precompute each length-x cost, then repeat k DP layers where each prefix either skips its last position or takes the ending window.
Median optimality proves every window weight, and the prefix transition enumerates exactly all non-overlapping selections.
editorial: Median optimality proves every window weight, and the prefix transition enumerates exactly all non-overlapping selections.

tests.explanation: Choosing indices 1..3 and 5..7 costs five and three changes, totaling eight.
The two adjacent -2 pairs can be formed with three total changes.
